column1: # Shared navigation-policy vectors for the desktop (Rust) and Android (Kotlin)
# Consumers (both load THIS file, neither has its own copy of the vectors):
# Format: tab-separated, one vector per line, '#' starts a comment, blank lines
# are ignored. A TSV rather than JSON on purpose: the pure Kotlin source set has
# no JSON parser (org.json is an unmocked stub in Android unit tests) and the
# Rust side would need a serde feature for one fixture, so both sides parse this
# with three lines of code and no dependencies.
# `url` vectors are TOP-LEVEL navigation decisions (`on_navigation` on desktop,
# `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` on Android). They are NOT a sub-resource policy:
# `data:image/...` is a legitimate source and stays untouched — only a
# top-level data: document is refused. `blob:` stays allowed because MSE players
# navigate the main frame to blob object URLs.
# `host` vectors go through Rust `is_private_host` and Kotlin
# blocked). `ip` vectors go through Rust `is_public_ip` and Kotlin
# `IpPolicy.isPublicIp`. Both follow the IANA IPv4/IPv6 Special-Purpose
# registries, fail closed on anything unparseable, and must agree on every line
# --- schemes: only https is a real navigation, plus the narrow media cases ----
# --- numeric host forms: the url crate normalises, Android's Uri does not ----
# --- public destinations must not be over-blocked ---------------------------
